name: Solenne Mirrorweave Spire Gala Gown
manufacturer: Solenne House (Spire exclusive, no public storefront)
description:
Solenne House does not advertise. It does not have a public address. Clients are introduced through existing clients, and the waiting period for a first consultation is measured in seasons. Their mirrorweave gown is the garment against which all other formal wear in GLMZ is implicitly measured, whether the people measuring it know the name or not. The fabric is a proprietary Solenne textile — holographic thread woven at a density that creates a surface which reflects and refracts light as if the gown is made of slow-moving water, shifting from silver to deep violet to colorless depending on viewing angle and ambient light source. The effect is not decorative. It is architectural. The gown does not fit into a room; it reorganizes the room around itself.

Beneath the holographic surface, the construction is a privacy-weave base layer that blocks passive biometric scanning, thermal imaging, and BCI handshake attempts — the Spire equivalent of discretion. Every closure, every seam, every accommodation for augmentation, geneware modification, or prosthetic is invisible from the outside. The gown has no visible openings because Solenne's atelier has hidden all of them so completely they don't read as openings at all. Price is not published. The Φ5,800 figure circulates as a floor estimate among Tier 4 observers who have never been in the same room as one.
cultural_context: Solenne gowns appear at the highest tier of GLMZ social life: Spire charity events, corponation board investitures, diplomatic receptions where the guest list itself is classified. The privacy-weave base layer has made the gown quietly controversial — it is, technically, a biometric countermeasure, which in some jurisdictions requires disclosure. Spire legal teams have ensured the relevant jurisdictions have been adjusted accordingly.
story_hooks: A Solenne gown is found abandoned in a Tier 2 transit locker — either its owner fled something, or someone wanted it found in exactly this location.
The privacy-weave base layer in a Solenne gown is blocking a Lazarus emergency medical alert from reaching first responders; the wearer is in distress and no one's scanners are registering them.

A Shelf-born character who has recently ascended through extraordinary circumstances is gifted a Solenne gown for a Spire event — and has to navigate a room full of people who know exactly what it cost and are watching to see if they know how to wear it.
